original_question: Let C~^2(D_d) be the class of twice continuously differentiable functions f on an open set D_d\subset R^d with volume 1 such that ||f||_infty <= 1, Lip(f) <= d^{-1/2}, and every directional derivative D^Theta f satisfies Lip(D^Theta f) <= d^{-1} for all directions Theta on the unit sphere. Does there exist a constant C>0, independent of d and of the domain D_d, such that the worst-case integration error always satisfies e(n,C~^2(D_d)) >= C n^{-2/d}?
target_in_paper: Section 4 ("General Domains"), Example 1, equation (14): the conjectured explicit uniform lower bound for deterministic numerical integration on the orthogonally invariant class \widetilde C^2(D_d), introduced immediately after Remark 8.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the correct target very closely: it identifies the right function class \widetilde C^2(D_d), the normalization \lambda_d(D_d)=1, the directional-derivative Lipschitz constraint, the uniformity of the constant with respect to both d and the domain D_d, and the exact lower-bound scale e(n,\widetilde C^2(D_d))\ge C n^{-2/d}. This is precisely the conjectural lower bound posed in Example 1.
missing_details: The paper’s e(n,F_d) is the minimal worst-case error over all deterministic algorithms that approximate \int_{D_d} f(x)\,dx using n function values; this should be stated explicitly.
The Lipschitz seminorm is defined by Lip(g)=sup_{x,y\in D_d} |g(x)-g(y)|/\|x-y\|_2, i.e. with the Euclidean norm.
D^\Theta f must be explicitly defined as the directional derivative in direction \Theta\in S^{d-1}.
The quantifiers should be made explicit: for all d,n\in \mathbb N and all open sets D_d\subset \mathbb R^d with Lebesgue measure \lambda_d(D_d)=1.
The functions are real-valued: f:D_d\to \mathbb R.
The conjecture belongs to the orthogonally invariant variant discussed in Remark 8; the paper emphasizes that only the case k=2 is treated there.
No additional boundary regularity is assumed here beyond D_d being open and volume-normalized; one should not add Lipschitz-domain assumptions.
The paper phrases this as an explicit uniform lower bound for integration, not as a broader tractability or asymptotic-constant problem.
refined_question:
Let d,n\in \mathbb N, and let D_d\subset \mathbb R^d be an open set with Lebesgue measure \lambda_d(D_d)=1. Define
\widetilde C^2(D_d):=\{f\in C^2(D_d;\mathbb R): \|f\|_\infty\le 1,\ \operatorname{Lip}(f)\le d^{-1/2},\ \operatorname{Lip}(D^\Theta f)\le d^{-1}\ \text{for every }\Theta\in S^{d-1}\},
where D^\Theta f denotes the directional derivative in direction \Theta and \operatorname{Lip}(g):=\sup_{x,y\in D_d,\ x\ne y}|g(x)-g(y)|/\|x-y\|_2. Let e(n,\widetilde C^2(D_d)) be the minimal worst-case error of deterministic algorithms that approximate \int_{D_d} f(x)\,dx using n function values. Is it true that there exists a constant C>0, independent of both d and D_d, such that
 e(n,\widetilde C^2(D_d))\ge C\,n^{-2/d}
for all d,n\in \mathbb N and all such domains D_d?
justification: The draft is targeting Example 1 in Section 4, not one of the paper’s earlier lower-bound statements for the non-rotationally-invariant classes F_d^k(D_d). Remark 8 introduces the orthogonally invariant norm and says that only the case k=2 will be discussed next; Example 1 then defines \widetilde C^2(D_d) exactly with the bounds \|f\|_\infty\le 1, Lip(f)\le d^{-1/2}, and Lip(D^\Theta f)\le d^{-1} for all \Theta\in S^{d-1}, and states the conjecture e(n,\widetilde C^2(D_d))\ge C n^{-2/d}. The introduction supplies the meaning of e(n,F_d) as the optimal deterministic worst-case integration error based on n function values. The surrounding comments in Example 1 explain that this would be an explicit uniform lower bound and that, because matching upper bounds are known for cubes, the rate n^{-2/d} cannot be improved. So the refined question above is the paper-faithful stand-alone version of exactly that conjecture.
